contents.reason: The complemented-subspace estimate is a separate structural application of bounded inverse and is not used by the Baire-principles chain, its norm corollary, or any selected example.

Theorem 4.1 — Baire theorem

Corollary 4.4 — Uniform Boundedness Principle
Fourier-series divergence discussion after Corollary 4.4
contents.reason: The Fourier partial-sum application needs the separate Fourier convergence and kernel conventions; no theorem in this Baire-principles pair uses Fourier coefficients or convergence modes.

contents.name: Theorem 4.5 — Open Mapping Theorem
Theorem 4.6 — Inverse Mapping Theorem
Examples following Theorem 4.6 — diagonal maps and failure of surjectivity
contents.reason: These sequence-space examples concern spectrum and range behavior rather than a Baire principle; they are not needed by the selected bounded-inverse proof or its planned companion leaves.

contents.name: Graph terminology for an operator
Theorem 4.7 — Closed Graph Theorem
Closability definition and the vertical-sequence criterion
Example — multiplication by j on a proper sequence-space domain
contents.reason: This is a sequence-space operator example distinct from the chosen differential operator; retaining both would enlarge the companion without adding a needed proof ingredient.

contents.name: Examples — nonclosable summation and point evaluation operators
contents.reason: The pair establishes the exact positive closability criterion and one closed unbounded example; the two negative domain examples require separate topology and dual-space context not used here.

contents.name: Lemma 4.8 — closure and inverse relations
contents.reason: Closure/inverse identities become load-bearing only when later unbounded operators and their adjoints are developed; neither the closed-graph proof nor the basic sequential criterion on this page invokes them.

contents.name: Corollary 4.9 — closed range and inverse on the range
contents.reason: The range formulation belongs with annihilators, adjoints, and quotient/range duality; it is not a prerequisite for the selected closed-graph theorem or its examples.

contents.name: Corollary 4.10 — quotient formulation of closed range
contents.reason: This quotient-range statement requires the later dual and quotient-space language in its intended use, while this page only needs the boundedness conclusion of the closed graph theorem.

contents.name: Corollary 4.11 — approximate range formulation
contents.reason: The orthogonality and closure-of-range consequences are planned with adjoints and annihilators; importing them here would create an unused branch beyond the Baire-principles route.

contents.name: Theorem 4.12 — Hellinger–Toeplitz theorem
contents.reason: Its symmetric-operator hypotheses and Hilbert-space conclusion are part of the later unbounded self-adjoint-operator route, not an ingredient of any theorem selected for this Banach-space page.

contents.name: Problem 4.1 — infinite-dimensional spaces have no countable Hamel basis
contents.reason: This algebraic dimension consequence is not used by uniform boundedness, open mapping, closed graph, or the chosen counterexamples, and needs its own Hamel-basis conventions.

contents.name: Problem 4.2 — a dense G-delta set of nowhere differentiable functions
contents.reason: The generic-function construction needs a separate function-space topology argument; it is not the condensation-of-singularities example chosen for this companion page.

contents.name: Problem 4.3 — uniform boundedness fails on c_00
Problem 4.4 — a dense G-delta in a complete metric space without isolated points cannot be countable
contents.reason: This category-set exercise is not required for the Baire theorem already published or for the functional-analytic consequences scaffolded in this pair.

contents.name: Problem 4.5 — continuity of Schauder coordinate functionals
contents.reason: The Schauder-basis coordinate-functional proof needs a basis and coefficient-space development; it is not a prerequisite of the selected Baire-principles theorems or c_00 counterexamples.

contents.name: Problem 4.6 — a compact symmetric operator on an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space is not surjective
contents.reason: This compact-operator and Hilbert-space conclusion needs spectral and compactness machinery outside the Banach-space Baire route, and no selected item applies it.

contents.name: Problem 4.7 — a bounded perturbation of a closed operator is closed
contents.reason: Closed-operator perturbation is a later unbounded-operator tool; the present pair defines and tests closedness but does not need a perturbation theorem to prove any selected result.

contents.name: Problem 4.8 — differentiation on C^1[0,1] has closed unbounded graph
Problem 4.9 — graph norms, completion, and closability
contents.reason: The graph-norm completion and closure identification are later unbounded-operator infrastructure; this pair proves only the basic sequential closability criterion and does not invoke graph-norm completion.

contents.name: Problem 4.10 — a closed plus nonclosable sequence-space operator can be closed
contents.reason: This specialized l2 operator-sum construction depends on the additional sequence-space examples and is not required to establish the chosen differential closed-operator example or the basic closability criterion.

contents.name: Remarks 3–4 — alternative proofs and the gliding-hump terminology

contents.name: Remark 7 — historical notes
contents.reason: The historical attribution is useful provenance but is not a mathematical result to be proved or applied on this page, so it is retained in the harvest rather than expanded into content.
